Samantha — attaching the MAP v3 draft and a concise deployment comparison table. High level: we see three viable lanes (Hosted, Dedicated, Private) and have sketched acceptance gates, cost bands, and a recommended pilot cadence for each.

Key asks for your team this week:
- Confirm which constraints matter most (data residency, VPC peering, encryption-at-rest KMS)
- Pick 1 primary region for the pilot (US East, US West, or EU-West)
- Agree to the evaluation window (we suggest 3 weeks for perf/latency and 4 weeks for stability/QA)

Acceptance criteria (proposed):
- 95th percentile token latency under 300ms for typical chat flows
- No functional regression on our eval prompt set (MAP eval v2)
- Successful secure key exchange and audit log ingestion into your SIEM

I'll sync with Ben and Laura on the Dedicated sizing estimate once you confirm the pilot region. If you'd like, we can do a short 30m call tomorrow to walk the MAP and tradeoffs.

Attachments: Aegis_MAP_v3.pdf, deployment_comparison_table.xlsx

—Markus

Thanks Mark — reviewed internally and good work on the MAP. A few clarifying points from our side:

1) Data residency: we need patient PII to remain in US-only regions. EU option is off the table for now.
2) Network: VPC peering with our AWS account is required for Dedicated and Private; Hosted needs a strict egress policy and IP allowlist.
3) Timeline: we have a board review on 14 Jul and want a vendor recommendation two business days prior (12 Jul). That means a MAP close by 9 Jul at the latest.

On mode: initial preference is Dedicated for predictability — but we need to see a cost delta and the canary plan (how you would run Hosted->Dedicated fallbacks during the pilot). Can you add a short canary/fallback section to the MAP?

Also looping Tom (Tech Lead) and procurement for timeline visibility.

—Samantha

Samantha — thanks for the clear constraints and the board timeline. We made the updates Laura requested and attached an updated MAP excerpt (Aegis_MAP_v3, page 6) with the canary/fallback play and two Dedicated SKUs (base, base+burst). Summary below:

Recommended pilot lane: Dedicated in us-east (primary) with Hosted us-west fallback for read-only traffic and low-latency reads during burst scenarios.

Canary plan (short):
- Day 0–3: Smoke tests in Dedicated staging with synthetic traffic; automated KV cache warm-up
- Day 4–10: Canary slice (5% of production traffic) routed to Dedicated in us-east; health checks on token latency, throughput, and error rates every 5 minutes
- Day 11–21: Ramp to 25% then 100% if no regressions; fallback policy auto-routes to Hosted us-west when 95th percentile latency breaches 450ms or error-rate exceeds 0.5% for 15m
- Rollback: immediate traffic shift to Hosted with postmortem within 72 hours; Dedicated capex commitment void until agreed remediation

Cost delta (quick):
- Hosted baseline: estimated $0.055 per 1k tokens (pilot profile)
- Dedicated (base): effective $0.032 per 1k tokens at monthly commit X (see spreadsheet)
- Dedicated (base+burst): $0.038 per 1k tokens with burst buffer included

Next steps we propose:
- Confirm pilot region (you indicated US East) by EOD Wed (30 Jun)
- Procurement to review the attached cost delta slide and proposed contract milestone for a 3-month pilot + option to convert to annual reserved capacity
- If you confirm region, we can schedule a 30m technical go/no-go on 6 Jul (engineers only) and provide a signed canary checklist before 12 Jul board packet

Attachments: Aegis_MAP_v3.pdf (updated), deployment_comparison_table.xlsx

—Markus
